title: Cartwise Shopper Batches Pay Components — Terms of Payment on Completed and Canceled Batches
content:
**1. Payment in components.** A completed batch of Cartwise Shopper Batches is paid in components. Each component is posted once per batch, or once per order for a per-order component, and each is rounded to the cent, half up.

**2. Where components may be posted.** Components are posted only on a batch that is completed or canceled, never on a dropped one. The batch's status is read from the system's batch record.

**3. The components.** Every figure named below is the batch type's schedule value.

| Component | Amount |
|---|---|
| Base pay | The batch type's base pay. |
| Per-order pay | The pay per additional order, multiplied by the orders in the batch beyond the first (a one-order batch has none). |
| Per-item pay | The pay per item unit, multiplied by the batch's item count, rounded to the cent. |
| Staging pay | The staging pay per order, for each staged order. |
| Mileage pay | The mileage rate multiplied by the part of the estimated route above the included miles (nothing when the route does not exceed them), rounded to the cent. It is always computed on the estimated route, never on actual miles. |
| Heavy pay | The heavy pay per unit multiplied by the batch's heavy units, when the batch type's heavy-pay starting figure is above zero and the heavy units are at least that figure. The heavy units are the quantities of charged item lines in the heavy category across the Cartwise Grocery Orders carried by the batch. |
| Waiting-time pay | The waiting rate multiplied by the recorded waiting minutes above the unpaid minutes (nothing when they do not exceed them), rounded to the cent, and then held at the batch type's waiting pay cap when it would exceed it. |
| Peak boost | The boost shown on the offer, where the batch type pays peak boosts, never above the batch type's largest peak boost. |
| Quality bonus | The quality bonus for each order rated 5 stars within the quality bonus window with no item refund. |
| Return pay | The return-to-store pay for each returned order. |
| Minimum top-up | When the sum of the components before tips is below the batch type's minimum batch pay, a top-up component brings it up to that floor. |

**4. Retired clauses.** The following two clauses of these terms are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis:

- the former clause under which the long-distance component was simply the batch type's long-distance bonus whenever the batch type's long-distance threshold was above zero and the estimated route exceeded it;
- the former clause under which, where the shown pay was a floor, a sum below the pay shown on the offer with no change to the orders after acceptance was owed as a shown-pay shortfall adjustment.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical batch and figures)

A hypothetical batch type pays a 0.50 mileage rate with 1.0 included mile, 0.15 per waiting minute above 15 unpaid minutes and a 6.00 waiting cap. A completed batch with a 7.3-mile estimated route and 33 recorded waiting minutes earns:

- mileage pay: 7.3 less 1.0 is 6.3 miles, multiplied by 0.50 is 3.15;
- waiting-time pay: 33 less 15 is 18 minutes, multiplied by 0.15 is 2.70, within the 6.00 cap.

Had the shopper driven 9.0 miles on that route, the mileage pay would still be 3.15, because it is computed on the estimated route.

superseded_clauses: long_distance is long_distance_bonus_usd when long_distance_threshold_miles is above 0 and estimated_miles exceeds it.
and when shown_pay_is_floor is true and the sum is below shown_pay_usd while the orders did not change after acceptance, the gap is owed as a shown_pay_shortfall adjustment.
